Horse Legal Guide

Horse Legal Guide is a free educational library of plain-English answers to equine law questions, covering horse sales, leases, boarding agreements, liability waivers, barn businesses and disputes. It explains how these situations usually work and what to check, and points readers with fact-specific problems to Wise Covington PLLC, an equine law firm.

A supporting educational surface designed to organize equine-law questions and route specific matters back to wisecovington.com.

What does equine law cover?

Equine law is the contract, liability, property and business law that applies to horses and the people who buy, sell, lease, board, train, insure and compete them. The most common questions fall into six groups: sale contracts and bills of sale, leases and trials, boarding and training agreements, injury liability and waivers, forming a horse business, and disputes over money or ownership.

Which equine laws apply in most states?

  • Horse sales are sales of goods under UCC Article 2; a sale of $500 or more generally needs a signed writing (UCC section 2-201).
  • Most states have an equine activity liability act that limits claims for the inherent risks of horses, usually only if a statutory warning is posted and included in contracts (Florida: Chapter 773).
  • Boarding stables in many states have a statutory lien for unpaid board, enforceable only after the notice steps the statute sets.

When do you need equine legal advice rather than a guide?

When money has already changed hands and the other side disagrees about what was promised, when someone has been hurt, when you have received a demand letter or a lien notice, or when you are about to sign something you cannot easily undo. Those turn on your documents and your state, and Wise Covington PLLC handles them.

Key facts and sources

  • UCC Article 2 governs horse sales in every state except Louisiana. (Uniform Commercial Code Article 2)
  • Florida's equine activity liability act is Chapter 773, Florida Statutes. (Fla. Stat. ch. 773)
  • A sale of goods for $500 or more generally needs a signed writing. (UCC section 2-201)

Questions people search

Where can I get equine law advice?

For general questions, the answers on this site explain how horse sales, leases, boarding, liability and business formation usually work. For a live dispute, injury or contract you are about to sign, contact Wise Covington PLLC, an equine law firm.

What is equine law?

The contract, liability, property and business rules that govern horses and the people who buy, sell, lease, board, train and insure them, including UCC Article 2 for sales and each state's equine activity liability act.

What horse laws apply in my state?

Every state but Louisiana applies UCC Article 2 to horse sales, and most states have an equine activity liability act with its own warning-sign and contract-language rules. The state guides on this site list the details.
